query: I need to implement register allocation for my compiler's x86-64 backend. I have ~15 virtual registers in my IR but only 14 physical GPRs available (excluding rsp/rbp). Linear scan vs graph coloring — which one for a compiler that prioritizes compile speed?

my compiler targets a stack-based bytecode VM. I'm getting stack underflow errors in some edge cases — I think the issue is how I generate code for short-circuit && and ||. The left operand pushes a value but the right operand might not execute. How do I handle this?

implementing instruction selection for ARM64 in my compiler. Should I use a tree-pattern matching approach (BURS/BURG style) or just write a big match statement on my IR nodes? The language is relatively simple — no SIMD, mostly scalar integer and float ops

I want to add NaN boxing to my bytecode VM for value representation. My language has doubles, 63-bit integers, bools, nil, and heap-allocated objects. How do I lay out the bit patterns? I've seen some VMs use the quiet NaN payload and some use the sign bit for tagging

my codegen emits correct code for simple functions but breaks on functions with more than 6 arguments. I think the issue is that I'm not handling stack-passed arguments correctly for the System V AMD64 calling convention. The first 6 go in rdi/rsi/rdx/rcx/r8/r9 right?

designing a register-based bytecode VM (like Lua 5.x or Dalvik). How many registers per frame is typical? And how do I handle function calls — do I need a separate register window like SPARC or just save/restore the caller's registers?

I need to generate machine code for closures and upvalues. My language has first-class functions with lexical scoping. The tricky part is that a closure might capture a variable that's still on the stack. Do I need to heap-allocate captured variables?

trying to emit WASM bytecode from my compiler instead of native code. The WASM type system is more restrictive than I expected — no arbitrary gotos, structured control flow only. How do I lower my CFG-based IR to WASM's block/loop/br structure?

what's the standard way to implement a dispatch loop for a bytecode interpreter? I'm using a giant match statement in Rust right now but I've heard computed gotos are much faster. Can I do something equivalent in Rust or do I need unsafe?

my compiler needs to generate code for tagged unions (sum types / enums with data). How should I lay out the discriminant + payload in memory? I'm targeting x86-64 native code and want to minimize padding. Should the tag be 1 byte, 4 bytes, or size-dependent?

I need to implement dead code elimination in my optimization pass. My IR is in SSA form. Do I use a mark-sweep approach starting from side-effectful instructions, or iterate to a fixed point removing unused definitions?
my parser isn't handling operator precedence correctly — `1 + 2 * 3` parses as `(1 + 2) * 3`. I think the issue is in my recursive descent rules for multiplicative vs additive expressions

I'm generating TypeScript code from a Protobuf schema. Using protoc with ts-proto plugin but the generated types don't match what the backend expects. Is there a better code generation approach for protobuf + TypeScript?
how do I use GitHub Copilot to generate boilerplate code faster? I'm writing a lot of CRUD endpoints and want the AI to fill in the repetitive parts

trying to implement garbage collection for my language runtime. I have a mark-and-sweep collector but it pauses for 50ms+ on large heaps. Should I switch to generational GC or try incremental marking?
what's the best approach for generating PDF reports from data in Python? I've tried reportlab but the API is really verbose. weasyprint looks nicer but has a lot of system dependencies

I need to implement the calling convention for my ABI — specifically how structs are passed by value. The System V AMD64 ABI says structs up to 16 bytes go in registers but I'm confused about the classification algorithm for structs with mixed int/float fields
how do I set up Terraform to provision AWS infrastructure? I need an ECS cluster with auto-scaling, an RDS instance, and an ALB. The Terraform docs are overwhelming

my linker is failing with 'relocation truncated to fit' errors. I think the issue is that my code section is too far from the data section for 32-bit PC-relative relocations. Do I need to use the large code model or add a GOT?

I'm building a source-to-source transpiler that converts Python to Rust. Not a full compiler, just translating the syntax — loops, functions, basic types. Should I work at the AST level or the token level?
